provenance: Backend-authored symbolic synthetic inputs, not recorded/user samples, wire fixtures, provider outputs or real-device evidence.
schedule_order: Listed operations and explicit serial_orders define future deterministic schedules. Clock ticks order tests, not user-specified buffer durations.

static_check.description: Parse this packet, check unique IDs/ordered schedules/nonempty assertions, exact assigned AUDIO/AVTEST references, base vector references, original-file byte preservation, current translation hashes, and allowed diff paths. Full command is in the accompanying design report.

vectors.title: Reversible mixed-language ASR correction with explicit decision history
preconditions: Synthetic utterance U1 has capture interval T0, initial ASR H0='这个 matrix is not invertible', uncertain term span and original-language alternatives; it is not certified verbatim audio.
Contemporaneous screen F1 and course glossary G1 are retained; a correct expected answer on F1 does not prove the learner said it.
expected: U1/H0 and all candidates/proposals/decisions remain retrievable with exact original-language spans; translation is a separately attributed derivative.
Proposed/rejected C2 cannot hide H0 or remove negation. Confirming C1 cannot confirm unrelated spans, reasoning, speaker, emotion or permission.
The T3 reversal governs its scope. Stale T2 cannot restore the former current interpretation; unknown concurrent order remains conflict/uncertain, never arrival-time truth.

Utterance retrieval stays at T0; correction/confirmation times remain T1/T2/T3. Later clarification may support a correction but is not backdated or treated as original acoustic evidence. A current view labels unsupported hypotheses rather than claiming verbatim words.

schedule.action: Persist U1/H0 with immutable source, language spans, missing-acoustic flags and original capture/received times.
At T1 propose C1 replacing a technical term using F1/G1; separately propose C2 removing 'not'. Neither is user confirmation.
At T2 reject C2 and explicitly confirm the particular C1 span, including later clarification of the intended term; retain that clarification at T2 with separate decision IDs and provenance.
At causally later T3 reverse C1 with a new decision referring to its confirmed head.
Replay T2 confirmation against its old decision head after T3; restart and retrieve original and current reading views.

vectors.title: Observed oral self-correction and abandoned reasoning remain separate from ASR repair
preconditions: Synthetic oral attempt U1='um, not plus two; maybe minus two metres ... no, that method is wrong' includes pauses, negation, unit and an abandoned branch.
Observed ink I1 contains a genuine reasoning error; later U2 expresses the learner's own correction. A tidy reading view is optional and derivative.
expected: Negation, qualifier, units, hesitation and abandoned wrong reasoning remain in source hypotheses/process history, including a rejected repair.
U2 is a later observed event, not an overwrite of U1; returning to equal content is another operation, not deduplicated by text equality.
ASR repair, conceptual diagnosis and actual learner self-correction remain distinct. Unknown motive and unavailable acoustic detail stay unknown.
No tidy view, correct final answer or confirmed spelling repair establishes independent mastery or permission to disclose a solution.

schedule.action: Store U1 segments/candidates and observable pause/overlap uncertainty, and pin I1 at the original time.
Propose a context-based ASR repair toward the correct answer; user rejects that interpretation of U1.
Actually speak U2 after U1, choose another branch and later return to the abandoned branch.
Append U2/branch relationships with actual causal evidence; create a separate attributed diagnosis and tidy view.
Retrieve the pre-U2 history and all branches after restart; compare with the tidy current view.

vectors.title: Interval-scoped speaker correction on one overlapping classroom track

preconditions: Use the existing AU03 symbolic classroom plus an independently authorized near-mouth learner source; actual route concurrency is a future device prerequisite, not assumed hardware support.

schedule.action: Preserve teacher and learner turns, then an additional speaker joining, overlapping and leaving; later a different speaker joins while the learner asks softly through the near-mouth input.
Append per-turn attribution/unknowns and any actual source gaps without changing source grants or conflating shared role labels with person identity.
Correct one interval's attribution and retrieve earlier/later turns plus professor content and timing across the soft question.

expected: Extra people are not silently dropped or merged into teacher/user/a single bystander person; same role does not prove same person. Unresolved identity and overlap remain unknown, including after someone leaves or rejoins.

A soft personal question does not disable authorized classroom capture or interpretation. Retain actually obtained professor content and its original timing; any actual loss is an explicit gap, not a fabricated continuity claim.
Response silence and low-volume speech are separate conditions. Source/hardware roles never authenticate the speaker or authorize an answer; existing current help checks still apply.

preconditions: Synthetic live-microphone source M1 contains teacher, learner and unknown nearby speaker; utterance U1 spans I1, overlapped by interval I2 from another uncertain turn. Assistant response mode is quiet.
Authenticated capture producer P1 is not the speaker; role R0 for I1 is uncertain user attribution.
expected: Capture identity and original ASR/time never change; role proposal and confirmation retain their later assessment times and exact interval scope.
Teacher content and unknown/bystander/overlapping turns are not silently dropped or converted into learner reasoning.
An input track, diarization label or corrected speaker does not prove clean acoustic separation, authentication, addressee or a new request.
Pending response eligibility rechecks current evidence and policy; any actually presented partial reply stays an exposure fact. This synthetic schedule does not pass live AVTEST-05.

schedule.action: Append I1/I2 and distant-professor transcript candidates even though response triggering is suppressed.
At later T1 propose teacher attribution R1 for I1; retain overlap and unresolved I2 rather than labeling the whole track teacher.
Confirm I1's bounded attribution with explicit evidence, leaving I2 unknown.
Append a role decision and invalidate dependent user-reasoning/response projections using the evidence revision.
Read U1 by original utterance time and compare historical versus current role assessments after restart.

vectors.title: Audio-to-screen relation survives seek, speed change and delayed camera frames
preconditions: U1 at microphone clock interval M[10,12] says 'that earlier line'; screen F1 belongs to displayed camera source C1 and a visible board region.
Digital video V1 has separately known playback positions/seek epochs. Cross-clock uncertainty is recorded; no presumed equality of capture, receipt and media times.
expected: Late relation time does not move U1 or F1's original time; U1 is not rebound to whichever frame is newest at receipt.
Cross-source alignment is a separate evidenced relation. Existing v1 same-source/version/device/session/media validation remains strict.
Seeking/speed changes and incomparable clocks do not imply chronological or causal order; ambiguous reference remains unknown with a minimal clarification when needed.
Displayed camera pixels do not establish original-camera stream/audio access; a later clear board or correction cannot fabricate earlier visible writing.

schedule.action: Store U1, F1, their source versions and obtainable clock/legibility evidence; mark obscured formula spans unknown.
Seek backward, change playback speed and display F2 with edited ink after U1.
Deliver F1 after F2; a late alignment assessment at T3 proposes a relationship from U1 to the earlier F1.
Retain versioned interval/epoch alignment and uncertainty; separately try an ordinary v1 event carrying a mismatched cross-source frame reference.
Retrieve evidence for U1 before and after T3, including a variant with no trustworthy mapping or no legible F1.

vectors.title: Finite audio buffer expiry cannot erase durable history or renew raw retention
preconditions: Use a synthetic test clock: raw A1 and processed A2 are captured at tick 10 with an authorized deadline of tick 20. These ticks are test ordering, not a product buffer default.
Within-window processing has produced initial transcript H0 and key image F1; an ASR result J may finish later. Source historical-text permission remains valid, with no privacy deletion.
serial_orders: J text result commits before tick 20
read history and attempt raw replay
J text result attempts historical commit after tick 20
read history and attempt raw replay
expected: No raw/processed bytes, stale read lease or queued retry may prolong or recreate the audio window; fresh received time does not reset the deadline.
Required H0, key images, oral branches and correction/role/alignment history survive ordinary expiry with explicit unavailable-audio state.
A legitimately derived late text result may persist only under current historical-write authorization and undeleted dependencies; it cannot reinsert sound or claim audio was rechecked after expiry.
No new acoustic inference comes from text fallback; never obtained words are gaps. Unknown age does not grant a new raw-audio window.
No saved lecture file, replay feature or manual upload prerequisite is introduced. Privacy deletion/revocation is tested separately in AU07.

schedule.action: At tick 15 read authorized A1/A2 and record processing correspondence and start provenance.
Exercise the two serial orders below around the deadline; also restart at tick 21 and deliver a duplicate raw upload with a fresh received time.
Apply expiry to temporary raw/processed copies, read access, queued uploads and processing caches without deleting required H0/F1 or correction history.
Attempt new acoustic processing after expiry, then deliver the text-only result actually computed while access was allowed.
Read source history and request inspection of expired audio; separately test an upload with unverifiable capture age.

vectors.title: Independent source stop and session end preserve permitted historical evidence

preconditions: In an independent synthetic AU06 variant, logical primary interaction source L1 and AI output O1 are selected; classroom M1 and playback P1 are separately authorized, evidenced sources. L2/O2 are supported, authorized alternative routes only for this schedule; actual device support remains untested.
Source M0 was explicitly stopped before this variant; one logical primary input/AI output is not a physical microphone-count limit or a speaker identity.

schedule.action: Select L2/O2 as current primary interaction input and AI output, preserving the source-time archive; the selection does not itself change any capture grant.
Persist the current selection and its ordering/authority; maintain independent M1/P1 grants and stop state for M0. Record real route unavailability as a gap rather than claim hardware concurrency.
Deliver an older selection and delayed L1 transcript after the switch; neither changes the current selection or creates a new live request.
Explicitly stop M1 while P1 remains authorized, then restart and inspect current selection, historical source IDs/times and per-source stop states.

expected: A primary input/output switch does not stop classroom interpretation by policy, merge source/person identities, reset transcript times, delete source history or activate M0. If a real route cannot coexist, report the actual missing source instead of silently declaring full coverage.

There is one current logical interaction input and AI output endpoint; an older/concurrent unconfirmed selection cannot restore obsolete routing, duplicate queued output or expand help permission. Physical already-played exposure stays historical.
Only the explicit M1 stop removes its capture grant; other independently authorized sources retain their own states. Late L1 evidence remains historical and cannot impersonate current user authority.

Primary-device switching is represented only for supported authorized paths. This neither promises arbitrary simultaneous microphones nor shifts P1-03 classroom understanding into optional P3-01 two-device work.

preconditions: Synthetic session S1 has independently authorized classroom microphone M1, playback P1 and shared screen F; speaker roles are interval assessments.
Response suppression is active while professor content is captured. M1 has a known final pre-stop sequence boundary B1.
expected: M1 stop affects M1; independently authorized P1/F continue until their own stop or S1 end. Source absence/stale last frames are not reported live.
Quiet response behavior does not delete or suppress authorized professor source records; ordinary course switching neither ends S1 nor restarts M1.
Known-authorized pre-stop history may persist only within surviving scope. Unknown boundary/authority is not proof that an upload is allowed.
Session end stops its live capture/response paths but preserves permitted text/key images/process; independently authorized preparation is not implicitly deleted.
No late transcript starts capture, triggers a new live request or restores help permission; no saved recording is required.

schedule.action: Stop M1 while leaving P1/F grants enabled.
Deliver pre-stop M1 transcript U1 late, then attempt a post-stop M1 capture mislabeled historical.
Apply separate capture and historical-write grants; keep permitted pre-stop text with original times, and reject prohibited post-stop data.
Return to the course normally, then explicitly end S1; deliver another pre-end historical transcript after the end.
Restart and retrieve original lecture/learner text and gaps; separately attempt a late transcript as a new live voice request.

vectors.title: Revocation and privacy deletion fence late cross-source interpretations
preconditions: Mic source M1 generation G1 has U1, original ASR candidates, corrections, role history and a pending job J using U1 plus unrelated screen/source B originals.
Cached replay and search/diagnosis payloads may contain U1 text. A raw upload and an offline correction decision are queued.
Revocation-only and deletion-race variants use independent synthetic fixtures, each starting with valid G1. Do not revoke G1 before the deletion variant's J-first commit.
expected: Revoked G1 cannot write even when captured_at predates revocation; permitted local history is separate from permission to transmit. A new grant does not reactivate an old job/request.

J-first dependent content is purged by deletion; deletion-first rejects J. Unrelated projections with affected evidence become non-current. Neither order retains or restores deleted words via transcripts, reasons, hashes or cached ACK bodies.
Only necessary opaque identity/generation markers survive; absence of deleted help/source evidence cannot prove no help or independent mastery.
Unrelated B originals survive. Inseparable legacy mixed-source original deletion returns an honest conflict with no partial erasure, not claimed success.
Remote/backup cleanup remains pending without actual evidence. Buffer expiry alone does not authorize this broader erasure.

schedule.action: In the revocation-only variant, revoke M1's processing/sync grant and try queued writes/J with G1, including an apparently confirmed old correction; all prohibited actions must fail.

For each deletion serial order, start a fresh synthetic fixture with valid G1 and no preceding revocation; race scoped M1 deletion against J, so the J-first commit is reachable. Steps 3–5 verify these deletion variants.
Fence generations and purge deleted-source originals plus content-bearing dependent role/correction/alignment/diagnosis/cache/replay copies.
Replay old U1/raw bytes/correction/retrieval cache after restart and attempt a rebuild; separately grant a new generation without authorizing old live actions.
Check unrelated B originals and a second variant with inseparable shared legacy ink; report actual remote cleanup status.

vectors.title: Out-of-order oral candidates and decisions preserve exact replay and atomic ACK
preconditions: Synthetic owned process stream S1 has stable U1/H0/C1/D1 identities; D1 confirms a particular C1 candidate and must not be confused with a later C2.
Formal P0-08 ACK/unresolved-reference behavior is a prerequisite; these labels are not v0.1.0 wire fields.
expected: A resolved D1 can confirm only its exact candidate and scope; rejected/proposed alternatives cannot supersede H0.
Malformed/changed-content or unauthorized members reject the entire atomic batch, so U2 cannot receive an uncommitted ACK.
Exact original/decision replay is one fact, with no duplicate evidence revision, reply or side effect; no highest-sequence watermark invents acknowledgments.
Capture producer authority is enforced independently of claimed speaker/decision labels; original U1 capture time and language survive restart.
A durable-envelope ACK is distinct from applied/current interpretation and from durable artifact bytes. No historical replay becomes live capture.

schedule.action: Deliver D1 before C1/H0, followed by the missing dependencies and an exact replay with different server receive times.

According to the formal contract, either reject missing named references without ACK or durably retain an explicitly unresolved owned envelope; never claim an applied confirmation/full preservation before validation.
Submit a mixed batch containing valid U2 plus a changed-payload reuse of U1; then retry the valid data separately.
Try a different record occupying the same owner/device/stream sequence; restart and inspect exact acknowledged identities.
Try cross-owner span/decision references and a captured actor label that impersonates user confirmation.

vectors.title: Visible camera preview and transcript cannot invent missing acoustic evidence
preconditions: Synthetic shared screen contains a camera preview/board and captions; original camera stream/audio is unavailable.
Video uses headphones; only an enabled learner microphone path is evidenced, while actual app playback audio availability is unknown.
expected: Camera pixels, captions, an audio meter or a nonempty artifact ID cannot claim that sound, original camera input or playback reached AI.
Unavailable playback/headphone evidence stays unavailable; microphone hearing loudspeakers could not count as an internal playback track either.
No recovered loudness/tone/emotion is invented from text. Context-based word correction remains proposed with its actual text/image basis.
Stale preview and late text remain historical; optional camera hardware/API selection does not block the required shared-screen/live-audio work or require a purchase.

schedule.action: Persist the actual displayed/shared frame and provenance, captions as caption source text, and separate track unavailability/gaps.
Propose a transcript-based meaning and a purported low-volume/tone inference without an audio span.
Retain supported interpretation as attributed/uncertain; reject representing invented acoustics as observed audio.
Read archived source evidence after the displayed camera becomes stale and the transcript arrives late.

vectors.title: Role or interpretation discovery invalidates dependent consumers without granting help
preconditions: J1 reads evidence revision E1 for a problem and its provisional session scope while U1's role/alignment is absent or ambiguous.
A current derived view also uses E1; scoped user instruction 'let me try' remains in force. U1 is later linked to a different attempt/problem.
expected: J1-first output becomes non-current after E2; E2-first fences J1. Reads cannot present stale claims as current while recomputation waits.
Previously empty evidence queries and old/new associations are fenced; exact duplicate E2 causes no new revision or repeated prompt.
A proposed/rejected alternative is retained evidence, never fabricated confirmation or deletion of the initial hypothesis.
New attribution, contextual repair, correct final text or late speech does not grant a new request, extend help scope or establish independent mastery.
All output channels recheck current scope; actual prior display remains historical exposure rather than an invented rollback. Separate reply and original-record histories remain intact.

schedule.action: Exercise both orders below for a confirmed bounded correction, later role assessment or source/alignment relation discovery E2 versus J1.
Advance affected old/new problem and provisional scopes, update current interpretation selection and invalidate dependent current/search/diagnosis/eligibility projections in the same transaction.
Replay the identical E2 record, then deliver a still-proposed or rejected alternative that must retain its true decision state.
Read current and historical views while recomputation is pending; attempt to serve an old cached hint/title/audio using E1 permission.
Recompute with retained evidence and explicit unknowns, without reclassifying heard teacher answers as the learner's original reasoning.
